newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Italian navy vessel rescued from Albanian sandbank.
newsitem.headline: Italian navy vessel rescued from Albanian sandbank.

text.p: The Italian navy flagship was freed from a sandbank off the southern Albanian port of Vlore on Wednesday, ending a humiliating incident for the eight-nation force security force protecting aid to the Balkan nation.

The Vittorio Veneto, a cruiser and helicopter carrier, was dislodged from the sandbank about 500 metres off shore at about 6 a.m. (0400 GMT) on Wednesday, more than 24 hours after the enormous grey ship had run aground in stormy seas. The Italian navy said the ship's anchor did not hold.

"The operation was completed early this morning and the ship is at sea," an Italian military spokesman said. "At this moment checks are being made to see if there is damage. The inspection will continue."
The Vittorio Veneto, which has been serving as the command centre for the U.N.-backed force in violence-stricken Albania, was pulled by tug boats off the sandbank and about 2,000 metres out to sea.

Four tugs had tried unsuccessfully to pull it from the sand on Tuesday. Two helicopters flew overhead, three small Italian naval boats circled nearby and divers in dinghies criss-crossed the water around the ship, which was listing slightly.
News of the Italian navy's problems brought a brief respite for Albanians, weary of more than two months of anarchic violence that has claimed more than 300 lives and left 700 injured.
"I thought they brought maps," said one man in Vlore, laughing. "This must be very embarrassing for the Italians."
"A cruiser finds itself enslaved by the Albanian coast," read one headline in the independent Gazeta Shqiptare daily.

The newspaper quoted local Vlore officials who complained that the Italians refused to accept assistance from the Albanian coast guard. "This is a violation of maritime laws," the paper quoted a Vlore official saying.

Vlore is controlled by a rebel committee, which rejects the authority of President Sali Berisha whom it blames for the collapse of fraudulent investment plans in which many Albanians had invested their life savings.

The eight-nation security force continued to grow on Wednesday. More than 4,000 soldiers from Italy, France, Greece, Spain, Romania and Turkey are already in Albania. Austria and Denmark will also send troops.
Romanian soldiers were expected to arrive in Gjirokaster, Albania's southernmost town on the Greek border. Early last month there were violent clashes in Gjirokaster after army weapons were looted.
The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) planned to distribute another three tonnes of food and medical supplies to hospitals and orphanges in southeastern Albania on Wednesday.

"We have had some worrying reports that the situation is dire in some remote parts of the country," said ICRC spokeswoman Nina Winquist-Galbe. "Some of these areas can only be reached by horseback and the food supplies are said to be quite low."
